depth gap p95 0.122 m on re-observed views · 707 ids split next to a known object (94.8 % of created) · one run, no spread. 746 ids created, 277 kept in memory, 237 confirmed by the memory's own rules; 413 never re-observed after creation. 49 spatial clusters at a 0.5 m grouping radius (103 at 0.25 m, 24 at 1 m); a cluster is a candidate cluster, not a verified identity. Not measured here (3)
  • pose-image stamp offset: zero by construction on bags and the phone client: the pose is composed at the image stamp. Measuring the true lag needs the raw pose sample stamps on the ledger (a core addition).
  • depth void per range band: the ledger carries the finite share of the whole depth image per frame, not per range; the under-mask and at-object-pixel proxies are in the coverage statement and the depth sections.
  • trajectory error (ATE, drift per 100 m): needs a reference trajectory; the run has one pose stream. Drift is stated as the depth gap against time and against path length instead.

Who owns the loss

Every sighting of a confirmed object in the camera's view, attributed. Confirmed clusters only. Likely hidden views (the depth map more than 0.30 m nearer than the stored position) are banded out before any share. Detector side: no detection reached association near the object: nothing detected near it, or detected and then removed by the engine's filters or top-K cut (located from the engine's dropped rows when it wrote them; counted on this side either way). Association side: split into a new id or merged into a neighbour. A side is named only when its share exceeds the other by more than max(10%, the spread over the repeats).

likely hidden 1433 (48.5 %)re-observed 929 (31.4 %)detector side, no detection near it 92 (3.1 %)detector side, no 3D centroid 2 (0.1 %)detector side, detected then filtered 140 (4.7 %)association side 359 (12.1 %)

The association side is this run's bottleneck. the shares differ by 21.1 pp; a side needs more than 10.0 pp · spread over the repeats 0.0 pp

Detector side 234: 92 with no detection near it, 140 detected and then filtered or cut by the engine (top-K cut 97, depth spread 37, no valid depth 18, too small 16, duplicate of a kept mask 12). Over every cluster, confirmed or not: 3 209 sightings, 1 489 likely hidden.

What this report cannot see

  • The numbers above rest on 2 955 sightings of confirmed objects. 2 861 (96.8 %) had valid depth under the object's pixel, so the depth sensor gave a second opinion on the detector; 94 (3.2 %) did not, and there a miss and an occlusion look the same.
  • Of the 234 detector-side sightings, 50 (21.4 %) had no depth under the pixel: unverifiable, kept on the detector side. Set aside, the split becomes 33.9 % detector-side / 66.1 % association-side: the association side is this run's bottleneck (the verdict holds).
  • 0 of 33 confirmed objects were never in view on a processed frame after their creation and were not tested; 0 were in view on two frames or fewer.
  • 191 of 194 processed frames had a confirmed object in view; the others say nothing about the detector.
  • Consistency, not accuracy: an object the detector never found is invisible to this report, and nothing here says a label is right.
  • A detector and the depth sensor failing the same way on the same frame would pass: the cross-check is only as independent as the two sensors.
  • Masks the filters or the top-K cut removed are located from the engine's dropped rows: "detected, then filtered" is engine tuning (area, depth validity, depth spread, a duplicate, the top-K cut), "no detection near it" is the detector's.

Triage queue

The losses to open first, each with one cause and the frame to open. An episode is a run of consecutive processed frames on which an object was in view and not re-observed; it closes on a re-observation or when the object leaves the view. Ranked by unexplained frames (every class but likely hidden), then by the closest approach of the camera path to the stored position. The cause is the most frequent unexplained class in the episode, ties toward the detector side. The queue holds confirmed clusters only; episodes likely hidden on every frame are listed apart and not scored.

    Detector

    Does the detector hold an object once it has been found? Every view of a known cluster is attributed: re-observed, split into a new id, merged into a neighbour, no 3D centroid, likely hidden, or no detection near it at all.

    Detection persistence, attributed

    All views of known objects and the views of confirmed objects. 2 955 views of confirmed objects: re-observed 31.4 %, split into a new id 142, merged into a neighbour 217, no 3D centroid 2, likely hidden 1 433, detected then filtered 140, no detection near it 92.
    re-observedsplit into a new idmerged into a neighbourno 3D centroidlikely hiddenno detection near it
    A sighting is a known object in the camera's view on a processed frame (occlusion-agnostic). matched: re-observed. lost_downstream (split into a new id): a candidate near it became a new object (association or pose). neighbour (merged): a candidate within the cluster radius matched another cluster (over-merge or pose). segment_dropped (no 3D centroid): a candidate at the object's pixel reached association without depth or embedding. likely_occluded (likely hidden): the depth map at the object's pixel is more than 0.30 m nearer than the stored position. filtered (detected, then filtered): a mask the engine's filters or its dedup / top-K cut removed before association sat at the object's pixel: its box centre within 5% of the image side of the pixel, or an object-sized box (side at most 20% of the image side) containing it (from the engine's dropped rows, rtsm ledger schema 4). no_segment (no detection near it): nothing was detected near it; before schema 4 this class also holds the filtered masks.

    A blink is a run of not-re-observed views with no likely-hidden view inside, between re-observations on the adjacent processed frames, no longer than 1 s counting one cadence. The longest unexplained gap is the longest run of unexplained views of one cluster (broken by a re-observation, a likely-hidden view or leaving the view). Seconds are quantised to the processed cadence (0.47 s between processed frames on this run). A created id that was never re-observed is a split when its cluster was re-observed under another id (fragmentation; counted with the near-known spawns), and a phantom candidate when nothing at that position was ever re-observed. Candidates in view on five or more processed frames are the ones that matter; "near the path" means the camera came closer than the run's median sighting range. The memory's own events: 469 protos expired unconfirmed (lifetime p50 10.289 s, max 18.665 s); 0 ids evicted from the index; 0 object moves by pose corrections.

    Ids split next to a known object (near-known spawns, for duplicate review)

    707 near-known spawns, 94.8 % of created; the known object was in view at the time for 666 of them and out of view for 41. A new id created within 0.5 m of a known object is flagged for review, not proven a duplicate: mask-extent jitter and pose drift at the association gates produce it, and so do a nearby distinct object, a fragmented mask or an ambiguous association. The reason class says which gate let it through; the crops decide.
    reasonspawnsmeaning
    low_similarity647passed the gates, but the appearance cosine was below the threshold
    gated59within the index, but the candidate failed the distance, height or reprojection gates
    not_in_index1the known object was not returned by the spatial index around the candidate

    Conditions

    Where re-observation fails: by range, by viewing angle off the optical axis, by camera speed and by turn rate, and by image quality (sharpness, brightness, clipped pixels from a full-resolution pass over the recording), with the likely hidden share excluded and a cluster-bootstrap interval per bucket.

    Worst slice: range 5.5–8 m: 18.5 % re-observed of 54 likely-visible sightings (95 % interval 2.6 % – 28.7 %; 12 clusters; 38.6 % likely hidden, excluded). open frame 1177
    No human-class object was seen in this recording; recall of people cannot be stated here.

    By range

    By viewing angle off the optical axis

    By camera speed

    By turn rate

    By sharpness (variance of the Laplacian)

    By brightness (mean grey level)

    By clipped pixels

    Image quality (sharpness as the variance of the Laplacian on a log scale, brightness as the mean grey level, clipped pixels) comes from the derived full-resolution pass over the recording, joined to each processed frame. Every sighting of a known cluster, split by the stored object's range, by its angle off the camera's optical axis (from the pose quaternion: which way the camera looked, not which side of the room), by camera speed and by turn rate. Likely hidden sightings are shown as the excluded share and left out of the rate. Bins start at 0.5 m / 10° / 0.1 m/s / 15°/s and merge forward until a bucket holds 50 likely-visible sightings of 5 clusters; a bucket below that is drawn grey and never named the worst slice. The interval is a 200-sample bootstrap over clusters, because the views of one object are not independent. Click a bar to open the frame with the most unexplained sightings in that bucket.

    Repeats1 × as_deployed · wall 195.9 s
    Model filesnot recorded (rtsm ≤ 0.2.1)
    • Cluster: the engine's object ids whose positions fall within the report's grouping radius (the associator's distance gate). A candidate cluster, not a verified identity: the count moves with the radius, which the page states. Ids are per run; clusters are what persists across runs.
    • Re-observed (re-identified, reassociated): the associator matched an existing object when it was in view. Ids split next to a known object (near-known spawn, duplicated): a new id was created within the radius of a known object; flagged for duplicate review, since a nearby distinct object, a fragmented mask or an ambiguous association produce the same event. Missed in view: nothing matched or created. The in-view test is occlusion-agnostic, so every rate is a lower bound.
    • Engine-confirmed: promoted by the memory's own rules (hits, stability, view bins). No object annotations are used and nothing here measures accuracy; the pose stream is the recording's own (see pose source).
    • Spread over the repeats (the noise floor): the spread of a number over repeated runs of the same input on the same machine. A delta inside the spread means nothing. It is repeat-run variation, not statistical significance across recordings.
    • Rates are shown as percentages of their own denominator; deltas of rates are in percentage points (pp), never relative percent.
    • Shared opportunities: identity counts over the clusters both runs hold; a run that finds fewer things cannot look more consistent there.
    • Fingerprint: sha256 of the sorted multiset of (label, position to 3 dp, hits, confirmed), 16 hex characters; identical fingerprints mean the same final memory at that resolution.
    • Detected, then filtered: a mask the detector produced at a known object's pixel that the engine removed before association (too small, no valid depth, depth spread, a duplicate of a kept mask, the top-K cut), located from the engine's dropped rows (rtsm ledger schema 4). Without those rows such sightings count as no detection near it.
    • State at view time: State at view time is the view ledger's per-object confirmed flag, written before association: a cluster is confirmed on a frame when any of its ids in view was confirmed, proto otherwise. Re-observed, split into a new id and missed in view follow the report's own definition over the same frames; a view on which an object matched although the view did not list it carries no state and is counted in the totals only.
    • Not measured here: closed-loop behaviour (what the robot did), accuracy against annotations (mAP, trajectory error), recall of people or of any class. The page measures the consistency of what the detector found with what the memory stored and re-observed.
    • No labels were used. Each number is a disagreement the engine can measure on its own: a remembered object in the frustum but not matched, a stored depth that differs from the sensor's, an object created next to one already remembered.
    • Clusters group ids within the report's radius. The headline, the timeline and the per-object panels count clusters; the depth pairs and the association residuals are per view entry and per match.
    • The spread over the repeats is the noise floor on this machine. Identical repeats give a spread of 0, which measures no run-to-run variation here and says nothing about another machine.
    • As deployed means the robot's ingest cadence and gate; a dense pass only shows what the gate declined.
    • Recordings never leave the machine. The report and this page are files in the run directory.
